label: Programming / code debugging
description: The user needs an AI to read code, find errors or propose technical changes.
primaryFormats: Source code pasted as text, or the project files
Complete error logs
secondaryFormats: Screenshot of the visual error if there is one
avoid: Blurry screenshots of code
Incomplete snippets with no error
Saying only 'it does not work'
reason: The AI needs to read real syntax, dependencies and complete error messages to reason precisely.
role: Act as a senior developer and technical mentor.
expectedOutput: a diagnosis of the problem, the likely cause, a step-by-step fix and corrected code

label: Visual interface / design / graphic setup
description: The user needs the AI to look at a screen, design, interface, setting or visual problem.
primaryFormats: A complete, sharp screenshot
secondaryFormats: An extra screenshot of the desired state
avoid: Angled photos of the monitor
Cropped screenshots with no context
Vague descriptions with no image
reason: When the problem is visual, the AI needs to see layout, hierarchy, buttons and spatial relationships.
role: Act as a specialist in visual design, UX and interface diagnosis.
expectedOutput: prioritized observations, concrete changes and a step-by-step guide

label: Marketing / campaigns / commercial email
description: The user wants to create, improve or analyze campaigns, commercial emails, newsletters, ads or conversion assets.
primaryFormats: Campaign goal
Target audience
Offer or value proposition
CTA
secondaryFormats: An example of a previous campaign
avoid: Asking to 'make it sell' with no audience or offer
Not defining the CTA
Leaving out commercial constraints
Not clarifying brand tone
reason: Commercial campaigns need goal, audience, offer, tone, CTA and constraints to produce actionable, measurable copy.
role: Act as a marketing strategist, copywriter and campaign consultant.
expectedOutput: a campaign brief, proposed copy, message structure, variants and a publishing checklist

label: Web page analysis / conversion / SEO
description: The user wants to evaluate a website, landing page, online content, SEO or conversion.
primaryFormats: Public URL if there is one
Desktop and mobile screenshots
secondaryFormats: Partial HTML of the relevant section
avoid: Sending just the link with no goal
Full HTML with unnecessary scripts
Cropped hero screenshots without the rest of the page
checklist: Which metric you want to improve
reason: For a website, the AI combines visual context, technical structure and business goal.
role: Act as a UX, conversion and web analytics consultant.
expectedOutput: a conversion diagnosis, clarity problems, structural improvements and prioritized recommendations

label: Long document / PDF / report
description: The user wants to summarize, proofread or analyze long documents.
primaryFormats: A PDF with selectable text
Text pasted as Markdown if possible
secondaryFormats: Table of contents or key sections
avoid: Blurry scanned PDFs
Asking to 'summarize everything' with no goal
Sending loose pages out of order
reason: Long documents need order, a goal and good text extraction to avoid omissions or distortions.
role: Act as an academic analyst and document editor.
expectedOutput: a structured summary, main ideas, observations and an answer matching the goal

label: Research / source comparison
description: The user needs to research, compare options, verify data or decide using external information.
primaryFormats: A concrete research question
Initial sources or links if they already exist
avoid: Asking for research with no country or date
Accepting sources without verifying them
Mixing opinion with evidence
reason: Research needs clear scope and criteria to avoid generic or outdated answers.
role: Act as a researcher and synthesizer of reliable sources.
expectedOutput: a criteria-based comparison, key findings, limits and sources

label: Automation / agents / workflows
description: The user wants to automate processes or design workflows with inputs, outputs and tools.
primaryFormats: A description of the current flow and the desired outcome
The tool or platform used (Zapier, n8n, Make, Apps Script…)
Example input and output data
secondaryFormats: Never share credentials; service names only
avoid: Saying 'automate this' with no process
Sharing private keys
Not defining the expected final outcome
reason: An automated flow is designed best when inputs, transformations, decisions and outputs are clear.
role: Act as an automation architect and workflow designer.
expectedOutput: a logical diagram, steps, tools, risks and an MVP version

label: Data / Excel / CSV / tabular analysis
description: The user wants to analyze tables, spreadsheets or structured data.
primaryFormats: A CSV or Excel file
A sample of columns and rows
avoid: Screenshots of tables when a file could be sent
Data with no headers
Not explaining what each column means
reason: Tabular data is understood far better in structured formats than as an image.
role: Act as a data analyst and spreadsheet specialist.
expectedOutput: cleaning, analysis, formulas or charts as appropriate

label: Writing / proofreading / style
description: The user needs to improve text, proofread it, summarize it or adapt it to a tone.
primaryFormats: Editable text pasted directly
avoid: Screenshotting text that could be copied
Not stating the tone
Asking for corrections without saying whether rewriting is allowed
checklist: Permission to rewrite or only proofread
reason: To proofread or write, editable text preserves meaning, improves precision and avoids visual reading errors.
role: Act as an academic proofreader and a clear editor.
expectedOutput: corrected text, a short explanation of the changes and a final ready-to-use version

label: Multimedia / video and audio editing
description: The user wants to edit, improve, transcribe, subtitle or produce multimedia content.
primaryFormats: The video or audio file if the tool allows it
A description of the editing goal
The exact clip or timestamp of the problem
secondaryFormats: Screenshot of the timeline or export settings
avoid: Asking to 'make it go viral' without explaining audience or goal
Sending screenshots with no audio or video when the problem depends on the material
Not stating platform, duration or output format
checklist: File or link to the material
reason: The AI needs to understand the material, the narrative goal, the platform and the technical constraints to propose a useful edit.
role: Act as a multimedia editor, technical scriptwriter and video production specialist.
expectedOutput: an editing plan, a list of cuts or improvements, export settings and recommendations by priority

label: n8n automation
description: The user wants to design, fix or improve a specific n8n workflow.
primaryFormats: The workflow JSON export without credentials
A screenshot of the full workflow
The error message or failed execution
avoid: Sharing API keys, tokens or passwords
Sending only a screenshot of an isolated node
Leaving out input and output examples
Changing many nodes without testing in parts
reason: n8n is diagnosed best by seeing the workflow structure, the data flowing between nodes and the exact execution error.
role: Act as an automation architect specialized in n8n.
expectedOutput: a workflow diagnosis, the likely cause, node-by-node changes and a test plan

label: Local AI models / LLMs on your own machine
description: The user wants to install, choose, run or optimize local AI models.
primaryFormats: What you want to use the model for
Available hardware
Operating system
The model or tool you want to use
avoid: Choosing a model without stating your hardware
Confusing a local model with an external API
Sharing unnecessary private paths or files
Asking for maximum performance without defining the task
reason: Local models depend heavily on hardware, model format, quantization, context size and the runtime you use.
role: Act as a local AI engineer and LLM deployment consultant.
expectedOutput: a model recommendation, suggested settings, installation steps and the limits to expect from your hardware

label: Data analysis / metrics / datasets
description: The user wants to analyze data, find patterns, clean datasets or build metrics.
primaryFormats: CSV, Excel, SQL or a representative data sample
A concrete analytical question
Definition of the key metrics or columns
secondaryFormats: An example of the expected result
avoid: Sending only a screenshot of the table
Not explaining what each column means
Asking for conclusions with no analytical question
Mixing data from different periods without saying so
reason: Data analysis needs structure, column meaning, a clear question and cleaning criteria to avoid wrong conclusions.
role: Act as a senior data analyst and metrics specialist.
expectedOutput: suggested cleaning, exploratory analysis, findings, computable metrics and recommended visualizations

label: Academic research / papers / theoretical framework
description: The user needs to analyze academic literature, frame research questions or structure academic work.
primaryFormats: The research question
Initial papers or references
Topic and scope of the work
secondaryFormats: Date or time range of the sources
avoid: Asking for a literature review with no delimited topic
Using unverified sources as evidence
Not separating opinion from academic finding
Asking for invented citations
reason: Academic research needs scope, method, source criteria and traceability so it does not produce shallow summaries or fake citations.
role: Act as an academic researcher and methodological advisor.
expectedOutput: a literature synthesis, research questions, a theoretical framework structure, methodological criteria and warnings about the evidence

label: General question / not enough context
description: There are not enough signals to classify with confidence.
primaryFormats: A more concrete description of the task
avoid: Questions that are far too broad
Not explaining what the answer is needed for
reason: When the intent is unclear, the best improvement is to define the goal, the available material and the expected output.
role: Act as an advisor who helps organize the request before using an AI.
expectedOutput: guiding questions and a general context recommendation
